solution: Solution: Depression in freezing point is given as $\Delta T = i K_f \times m$ where, $i=$ van't Hoff factor $K_f=$ molal freezing point depression constant $m = \text{molality}$ Molar mass of glucose $(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}_6)$ $=12 \times 6+12 \times 1+6 \times 16=180\ \text{g/mol}$ Molality of glucose $= \frac{\;\text{ Mass of solute }\;}{\;\text{ Molar mass of solute }\;} \times \frac{1}{\;\text{ Mass of solvent (kg) }\;}$ $= \frac{1.8}{180} \times \frac{1}{0.1} = 0.1\ \text{m}$ $\therefore \Delta T = 1 \times 1.86\ \text{K kg / mol} \times 0.1\ \text{m}$ $=0.186^{\circ}\ \text{C}$ $\therefore$ $\text{Freezing point of solution = Freezing point of water - Depression in freezing point}$ $=0^{\circ}\ \text{C} - 0.186^{\circ}\ \text{C} = \therefore 186^{\circ}\ \text{C}$ © examsnet.com
